front: Quand j'étais enfant, j'habitais dans un petit village.
pronunciation: [kahn zhay-teh tahn-FAHN, zhah-bee-teh dahn zan puh-tee vee-LAHZH]
back: When I was a child, I lived in a small village.
context: Childhood memories are told mostly in the imparfait.

front: Je me souviens de l'odeur du pain chaud le matin.
pronunciation: [zhuh muh soo-vyan duh loh-duhr dü pan SHOH luh mah-TAN]
back: I remember the smell of warm bread in the morning.

front: Je me rappelle très bien mon premier jour d'école.
pronunciation: [zhuh muh rah-pel treh byan mohn pruh-myay zhoor day-KOL]
back: I remember my first day at school very well.

front: Mes parents m'emmenaient à la mer chaque été.
pronunciation: [may pah-rahn mahm-muh-neh ah lah MEHR shak ay-TAY]
back: My parents used to take me to the seaside every summer.

front: Je passais des heures à lire des bandes dessinées.
pronunciation: [zhuh pah-seh day ZUHR ah leer day bahnd day-see-NAY]
back: I spent hours reading comics.

front: J'avais un chien qui s'appelait Rex.
pronunciation: [zhah-veh tan SHYAN kee sah-puh-leh REKS]
back: I had a dog called Rex.

front: Ma grand-mère me racontait des histoires avant de dormir.
pronunciation: [mah grahn-mehr muh rah-kohn-teh day zees-TWAHR ah-vahn duh dor-MEER]
back: My grandmother used to tell me stories before bed.

front: On jouait au foot dans la rue jusqu'à la nuit.
pronunciation: [ohn zhoo-eh oh foot dahn lah RÜ zhüs-kah lah NWEE]
back: We used to play soccer in the street until dark.

front: J'étais un enfant plutôt timide.
pronunciation: [zhay-teh zan nahn-fahn plü-toh tee-MEED]
back: I was a rather shy child.

front: Mon frère et moi, on se disputait tout le temps.
pronunciation: [mohn frehr ay MWAH, ohn suh dees-pü-teh tool TAHN]
back: My brother and I argued all the time.

front: À l'école, ma matière préférée était le dessin.
pronunciation: [ah lay-KOL, mah mah-tyehr pray-fay-RAY ay-teh luh deh-SAN]
back: At school, my favorite subject was drawing.

front: J'avais peur du noir.
pronunciation: [zhah-veh puhr dü NWAHR]
back: I was afraid of the dark.

front: Un jour, je suis tombé de vélo et je me suis cassé le bras.
pronunciation: [an ZHOOR, zhuh swee tohm-bay duh vay-LOH ay zhuh muh swee kah-say luh BRAH]
back: One day I fell off my bike and broke my arm.
context: 'Un jour' introduces a specific event → passé composé.

front: Ce jour-là, j'ai pleuré pendant des heures.
pronunciation: [suh zhoor-LAH, zhay pluh-ray pahn-dahn day ZUHR]
back: That day, I cried for hours.

front: Nous vivions dans un appartement au dernier étage.
pronunciation: [noo vee-vyohn dahn zan nah-par-tuh-MAHN oh dehr-nyay ay-TAZH]
back: We lived in an apartment on the top floor.

front: Le mercredi après-midi, j'allais au conservatoire.
pronunciation: [luh mehr-kruh-DEE ah-preh-mee-DEE, zhah-leh oh kohn-sehr-vah-TWAHR]
back: On Wednesday afternoons I went to the music school.
context: French children traditionally had Wednesday afternoons off.

front: Je rêvais de devenir pompier.
pronunciation: [zhuh reh-veh duh duh-vuh-neer pohm-PYAY]
back: I dreamed of becoming a firefighter.

front: Je ne mangeais jamais mes légumes.
pronunciation: [zhuh nuh mahn-zheh zhah-meh may lay-GÜM]
back: I never ate my vegetables.

front: Les vacances chez mes cousins, c'était le paradis.
pronunciation: [lay vah-kahns shay may koo-ZAN, seh-teh luh pah-rah-DEE]
back: Holidays at my cousins' were heaven.

front: Il n'y avait pas internet à cette époque.
pronunciation: [eel nyah-veh pah zan-tehr-net ah set ay-POK]
back: There was no internet at that time.

front: Je me souviens que ma mère chantait en cuisinant.
pronunciation: [zhuh muh soo-vyan kuh mah mehr shahn-teh ahn kwee-zee-NAHN]
back: I remember my mother singing while she cooked.

front: J'ai grandi en Normandie.
pronunciation: [zhay grahn-dee ahn nor-mahn-DEE]
back: I grew up in Normandy.
context: 'Grandir' = to grow up (passé composé for the overall fact).

front: Nous avons déménagé quand j'avais dix ans.
pronunciation: [noo zah-vohn day-may-nah-zhay kahn zhah-veh dee ZAHN]
back: We moved when I was ten.

front: Mes meilleurs souvenirs sont liés à la musique.
pronunciation: [may meh-yuhr soov-NEER sohn lyay ah lah mü-ZEEK]
back: My best memories are linked to music.

front: Ça me rappelle mon enfance.
pronunciation: [sah muh rah-pel mohn nahn-FAHNS]
back: That reminds me of my childhood.
context: 'Rappeler quelque chose à quelqu'un' = to remind someone of something.

front: Ça me rappelle des souvenirs !
pronunciation: [sah muh rah-pel day soov-NEER]
back: That brings back memories!

front: Je n'en garde qu'un vague souvenir.
pronunciation: [zhuh nahn gard kan vahg soov-NEER]
back: I only have a vague memory of it.
context: 'Ne… que' = only. 'Garder un souvenir' = to keep a memory.

front: Le Noël de mes huit ans reste inoubliable.
pronunciation: [luh noh-EL duh may wee TAHN rest ee-noo-blee-YAH-bluh]
back: The Christmas when I was eight remains unforgettable.
context: 'De mes huit ans' = when I was eight.

front: On faisait des cabanes dans la forêt.
pronunciation: [ohn fuh-zeh day kah-BAN dahn lah foh-REH]
back: We used to build huts in the forest.

front: Quand il neigeait, l'école fermait et c'était la fête.
pronunciation: [kahn teel neh-ZHEH, lay-kol fehr-meh ay seh-teh lah FET]
back: When it snowed, the school closed and it was party time.

front: Mon institutrice s'appelait Madame Leroy.
pronunciation: [mohn nan-stee-tü-TREES sah-puh-leh mah-dam luh-RWAH]
back: My primary school teacher was called Madame Leroy.
context: 'Un instituteur / une institutrice' (or 'un professeur des écoles') = primary teacher.

front: Je n'oublierai jamais ce voyage.
pronunciation: [zhuh noo-blee-reh zhah-meh suh vwah-YAHZH]
back: I'll never forget that trip.

front: Petit, j'étais très turbulent.
pronunciation: [puh-TEE, zhay-teh treh tür-bü-LAHN]
back: As a kid, I was very boisterous.
context: 'Petit(e),' at the start = when I was little.

front: J'ai eu une enfance heureuse.
pronunciation: [zhay ü ün nahn-fahns uh-RUHZ]
back: I had a happy childhood.
context: Overall assessment of a closed period → passé composé.

front: C'était une autre époque.
pronunciation: [seh-teh tün oh-tray-POK]
back: It was a different time.
